items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: He studied with a guy named George Tremblay.

ctx.x: And so he would, and all those guys do that kind of stuff. So he would recycle some stuff. But then he was always trying to find different stuff too. He studied with a guy named George Tremblay. And George Tremblay was working with Quincy and a lot of guys out there using twelve tone techniques. So he really got into serial composition and twelve tone techniques, and you know the retrograde and all that kind of stuff. He really © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

got into — if you look at his Patterns for Improvisation there’s a twelve tone row that he’s got. And I can’t remember what exercise it is now but I was just playing it the other day. So he really wanted to get into that. You know I’m going to digress one second. You said something that really would get him angry? One thing that would get him angry was being recognized not just as a jazz musician. And that would bother him. That bothered David Baker too. Because I mean David was a tremendous writer. He could…
